After commit prefer application rollback retaining additive columns/tables. Rehearse actual old app compatibility, including new uniqueness errors and marker warnings; compatibility is not assumed.

Restoring a production restore point may discard every later write. Test restoration on another branch and make an explicit incident decision.

plateUniqueness.databaseConstraint: Exact pair UNIQUE(companyId,plateNumber); separate companies may reuse the same plate.
plateUniqueness.applicationRule: VehicleInputDto trims/uppercases new plates. VehiclesRepository checks upper(btrim(plateNumber)) under a company-row lock, including padded legacy values.
plateUniqueness.preflight: Require zero exact and normalized duplicate groups. Do not repair, delete or renumber records automatically. Blank/overlong legacy plates require an explicit editing policy; reads preserve them.
plateUniqueness.limitation: The exact database constraint alone allows case/space variants from external writers. All fleet writers must use the approved repository; strict normalized uniqueness across arbitrary writers would require a separately approved contract/index change.

logical: Use a version-compatible pg_dump via a protected libpq service and password file outside this repository; never pass a connection URL/password on the command line.

After write quiescence, pg_dump --dbname=service=fleetora_live_backup --format=custom --file=<encrypted-volume>/fleetora-pre-vehicle.dump. Include public and prisma_contract; do not dump only vehicles.

Keep the archive on approved encrypted storage, access-restricted; record SHA-256 and pg_restore --list results privately. Password hashes/tokens in the archive make it sensitive. Never commit archive, connection settings, or DB query output.

Restore only to an empty, separately approved rehearsal database: pg_restore --dbname=service=fleetora_restore_rehearsal --exit-on-error --single-transaction --no-owner --no-acl <archive>. Reconcile required role ownership/ACLs separately before accepting the restore.
Verify all schema objects, counts, IDs, assignments, marker/ledger, app compatibility and separately reviewed grants. A successful pg_dump alone is not a tested restore.

remainingConcurrencyTests: Two different drivers race for one vehicle: exactly one succeeds, the loser receives 409 and its old assignment remains.
Concurrent replace/unassign/edit on the same driver: expectedVehicleId CAS protects against stale writes and stale unassignment; verify no lost update.
Concurrent normalized plate create/edit in one company: one succeeds; other company can independently reuse the plate. Include whitespace/case legacy values and external-writer limitations.
Actor role/company/active/verified status or company suspension changes while fleet write waits: persisted locked identity must deny the stale write.
Cross-company assignment attempts while another transaction assigns the same vehicle: no tenant leak or reassignment theft, unique constraint rolls back conflicts.

Exercise independent pooled/direct connections, transaction failures, deadlock/lock timeouts and disconnects; validate 409 mapping and no automatic replay of uncertain writes. PGlite single-session tests do not satisfy this gate.
